Fig. 3: Comparison of segmentation performance versus trainable parameter count across SOTA methods, averaged over five medical imaging datasets: BUS, BUSI, GlaS, HAM10000, and Kvasir–Instrument. (a) Trainable parameters vs. average DSC score. (b) Trainable parameters vs. average IoU score. (c) Trainable parameters vs. average HD95 score. Higher DSC and IoU (↑) indicate better overlap accuracy, while lower HD95 (↓) reflects better boundary precision. Blue circles denote CNN/Transformerbased models, and orange squares denote generative models. GET (Ours) achieves a favorable efficiency–accuracy trade-off, with top-tier DSC, IoU, and HD95 performance using substantially fewer trainable parameters than existing SOTA methods.
